'''James Moffat''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FIMA|CMath}} is a [[mathematician]]. He was a researcher for the Ministry of Defence during the 1982 [[Falklands War]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Ramo|first1=Joshua Cooper|title=The Age of the Unthinkable|date=March 23, 2009|publisher=Little Brown|pages=Chapter 9|url=https://archive.org/details/ageofunthinkable00ramo|url-access=registration|quote=james moffat mathematician.}}</ref> He wrote ''Complexity Theory and Network Centric Warfare'',<ref>{{cite book|last1=Moffat|first1=James|title=Complexity Theory and Network Centric Warfare|date=2010|publisher=Diane Publishing|isbn=978-1893723115|url=http://www.dodccrp.org/files/Moffat_Complexity.pdf|accessdate=11 September 2017}}</ref> which has 275 [[citation count|scholarly citations]].<ref>{{cite web|title=book citation count|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&q=James+Moffat&btnG=&as_sdt=1%2C5&as_sdtp=|publisher=Google Scholar|accessdate=21 September 2017}}</ref>

Moffat is currently Professor of Physics at the [[University of Aberdeen]], where he studies [[quantum gravity]]. He has published 135 articles.  He is a recipient of the Napier Medal in Mathematics and the President’s Medal of the ORS; the 'nobel medal in analytics'. He is also a Fellow of OR, a [[Fellow of the Institute of Mathematics and its Applications]], and a [[Chartered Mathematician]]. His contributions to the literature cited 560 times include new theories for [[Loop Quantum Gravity]] based on the Mathematics of [[Operator algebra|Operator Algebra]]s.<ref>{{cite web|title=Moffat, James|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/James_Moffat|accessdate=11 September 2017}}</ref>

Moffat was an early writer on the topic of the ''Agile Organization''.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Atkinson|first1=Simon|last2 = Moffat|first2=James|title=The agile organization: from informal networks to complex effects and agility|date=July 2005|publisher=Department of Defense|isbn=1-893723-16-X|url=http://www.dodccrp.org/files/Atkinson_Agile.pdf}}</ref> [[Business agility]], generally, had been discussed before, but agility, specifically in the context of military organizations, was a new field in 2005.
